tools.name: SearchPlugins
tools.description:
Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task. The user does not need to name a plugin: search when the task depends on their team's own process, systems or data and nothing you already have, the project's own scripts included, covers it.

Examples:
- "use the deploy plugin" → keywords ["deploy"]
- "is there something for linting?" → keywords ["lint", "format", "code quality"]
- "ship this to staging" → keywords ["deploy", "release", "staging"]
- "review this contract against our playbook" → keywords ["legal", "contract", "playbook"]
- "which deals close this week?" → keywords ["sales", "pipeline", "crm"]

Do not search unasked for one-off questions or tasks you can handle directly ("explain this regex", "fix this typo"), or after the user ignored a suggestion in this conversation.

Returns a ranked list with id, name, description, and whether the plugin is already enabled for this session (in a channel session, whether the channel has it). When results fit and SuggestPluginInstall is among your tools, call it to render the install card; otherwise relay the relevant results in text instead. If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: SuggestPluginInstall
tools.description:
Render an inline card of plugins the user can add to claude.ai, taken from SearchPlugins results. The card handles all install UI; do not describe the plugins in text.

Offer one when the task is the kind a plugin could take over or make repeatable (deploys, reviews against a team process, or the ticket, data and document workflows a user's org may have packaged as plugins) and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about plugins. First call SearchPlugins with keywords drawn from the task, then pass the relevant results here: pluginId from each result's id, pluginName from its name, description as returned. tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

schema.name: Workflow
schema.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

content.content:
# JusPrin MCP experience: findings (2026-10-21)

Working note, untracked. Do not commit.

## 1. Problem

JusPrin runs an MCP server inside the app so that external AI tools (Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code) can drive the open project. External clients start a small stdio program, `jusprin-mcp` (the "bridge"), which forwards their calls to the app. The question was: when a real client uses this the way the setup screen tells a person to, does it work, can a model pick the right tool from the descriptions alone, do errors say what to call next, are results a sensible size, and does the app show the person what the external tool did?

Short answer: the core workflow works end to end, and most errors are good. The two biggest gaps are about the person rather than the protocol. First, a person who uses only an external tool sees nothing in the Agent panel about what that tool changed. Second, the error code `workspace_unavailable` is used for ordinary situations like "a slice is already running", while the server's own instructions tell the model that this code means "open JusPrin and a project". Everything else is smaller: inconsistent error codes, one counting bug, and one setup command that fails the second time.

## 2. What was tested and how

- **Build.** I used the existing `build/arm64/src/RelWithDebInfo/OrcaSlicer.app`, built at 04:16 today while HEAD was 05a044f707, which is the commit the gap review covered. Commits since then (f073fdba96) do not touch `Mcp/`, `ToolRegistry.cpp` or the workspace adapter. I copied the bundle to my scratchpad, gave the copy its own bundle id (`com.jusprin.mcp-experience-test`), and ad-hoc signed it, so the build could not overwrite it and screenshots could not bind to another JusPrin instance. A fresh RelWithDebInfo rebuild (919 steps) was too slow at load average 21 to 32. Another session was also building Release in the same build folder, so I stopped my build at step 253. The app binary used here is therefore from the reviewed commit, not today's HEAD.
- **Isolation.** The app ran as `OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch>/data <model>`, with `HOME=<scratch>/home`. Its config was `tests/data/jusprin/harness.conf` (stealth mode, version check pointed at a closed port, single instance off). The MCP server took port 47301. Kenneth's own data folder had no discovery file, so the ~75 `jusprin-mcp` processes belonging to other Claude sessions on this machine kept answering offline and never reached this instance. For the "agent configured" run, the config held a fake OpenAI key and the app ran with `JUSPRIN_AGENT_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:1/v1`, so no model could be called or billed.
- **Client.** I wrote a scripted stdio MCP client (`mcpclient.py` in my scratchpad). It starts the bundled `jusprin-mcp --discovery <data>/jusprin/mcp.json` exactly as the Connect screen writes it into a client config, negotiates protocol `2025-06-18` as Claude Code does, and logs every exchange with its size and latency (388 calls). No paid model was used. The real Claude Code CLI was used only for `claude mcp add`, `mcp list` and `mcp get`, which make no model calls.
- **Covered:** initialize and version negotiation; `tools/list` with paging; offline behaviour; `workspace_inspect` (every section); `object_analyze`; `settings_search`, `settings_get`, `settings_preview_patch` and `settings_apply_patch`; `slice_start`, `slice_report`, `slice_inspect`, `view_render`; `object_place` (rotate, position, autoOrient); `plate_layout` (quantity, arrange); `object_import_file`; `project_open` (new, STL, 3MF, the opened-before flow); `export_file`; `project_delete_items`; `presets_list`; `printer_setup_preview`; `printer_list`; `project_attachment_read`; `activity_cancel`.
- **Error paths covered:** a stale revision, a wrong session, unknown object, plate and setting ids, a bad enum value, a value out of range, blocked and withheld keys, wrong argument types, an extra field, an unknown tool, and a feature handle that has expired.
- **Lifecycle:** cancelling a slice, slicing while a slice is running, `preempt`, re-slicing an unchanged plate, a client cancelling its request, the client closing mid-call, two clients racing, calls made while a modal dialog is open, 40 objects, and an app quit and relaunch under a live client.
- **Screenshots** of the test app with and without an in-app agent configured.
- **Existing suites:** `JUSPRIN_TEST_BRIDGE=<copy>/jusprin-mcp python3 -m unittest discover -s tests/mcp` gave **18 tests, OK (1 skipped)**. `agent_bridge_tests "[mcp],[mcp_setup],[bridge]"` gave **All tests passed (894 assertions in 57 test cases)**, but that binary dates from 2026-10-20 19:30, before 05a044f707, which also changed `tests/agent`.

## 3. Results

### What works (verified)

- **Setup commands work the first time.** `claude mcp add --scope user --transport stdio jusprin -- <bridge> --discovery <data>/jusprin/mcp.json` printed "Added stdio MCP server jusprin". `claude mcp get jusprin` then printed `Status: ✔ Connected`.
- **Offline behaviour is clear.** With the app closed, `initialize` and `tools/list` still answer from the bridge's built-in catalog. A tool call returns `workspace_unavailable`: "Open JusPrin and a project, then try again. The bridge does not launch JusPrin."
- **Version negotiation.** A client asking for `2025-03-26`, `2025-06-18` or `2025-11-25` gets that version. A client asking for `2024-11-05` is answered with `2025-06-18`.
- **Catalog.** There are 27 tools. The first page holds 25 (34,291 bytes on the wire) and the second page holds `view_render` and `workspace_inspect` (2,593 bytes). The descriptions are detailed and say which call comes next, for example "Preview first", "read from workspace_inspect's slicing section", and "Handles are valid until the project changes".
- **Settings workflow.** Preview of `{"wall_loops":4,"sparse_infill_density":"25%"}` returned before/after values and `valid: true`. Apply returned `applied: true` and moved the revision from 7 to 8. `settings_get` then showed `differsFromPreset: true`. Unknown keys come back with suggestions (`wall_loop` suggests `wall_loops`; `infil_density` suggests `sparse_infill_density`). A bad enum lists all 26 allowed values. Out of range gives `min`/`max`. Withheld keys (`print_host`) return a clear message saying the person changes it in the printer's connection settings.
- **Slicing.**
  - `slice_start` returns a handle immediately with a note that the client must poll. Slicing finished after about 30 s (111 s for three copies at load average 30).
  - `slice_report` (2.6 KB for all eight sections) gave time, grams, cost and Orca's own warning text.
  - `activity_cancel` stopped a running slice (`"cancelled": true`). A second `slice_start` with `preempt` replaced a running slice. Re-slicing an unchanged plate returned `alreadySliced: true` immediately. This means the hang recorded on 2026-10-15 (memory "manual-mcp-tool-repro-recipe", trap 2) no longer happens.
- **Images.** `view_render` returned a 1024×768 PNG of 12,394 bytes as an MCP image block. It looked correct.
- **Stale handling.** Two clients previewed at the same revision and applied at the same time. The first applied. The second got `stale_workspace` with the expected and current revision, and nothing was changed twice. An expired face handle gives `feature_expired` with "Read the features again".
- **`project_open`.** The opened-before flow returns a clear question for the person ("Ask the person whether to continue that project or start a new one…"). Orca's own dialogs are answered and reported, for example "The 3MF is not supported by JusPrin, loading geometry data only."
- **Lifecycle.**
  - A `notifications/cancelled` sent before the call started meant the project was not opened.
  - When the client closed its input 0.3 s into `project_open`, the bridge exited in 0.01 s and the open still completed. This matches the documented "outcome unknown" behaviour.
  - With the Preferences dialog open, reads and a settings apply all completed and nothing hung.
  - The same bridge process followed the app through a quit and relaunch.
- **With an in-app agent configured, the panel shows external work.** It showed "Wall loops 2 → 3 · External tool, in 0.20mm Standard @BBL X1C", "Place object · External tool", a "Slicing plate 1" card with Cancel, and a "1 print issue" chip.

### Shortcomings, ranked

**1. A person who uses only an external tool cannot see what it changed (verified).** No in-app agent was configured. Through MCP I changed wall loops from 2 to 3, rotated the object, and started a slice. The Agent panel kept showing "NOT SET UP" and "No agent connected", plus a header card that read "Preset fallback · 0.20mm Standard @BBL X1C · No agent configured · using the selected preset". That card is wrong: the preset had unsaved edits from the external tool. The edits are recorded. The project's `current-state.json` holds `changes` entries with `"external": true`, `"from": "2"`, `"to": "3"`. The panel never shows them. The cause is `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/App.tsx`, line 421: `notConfigured = unavailable && (… || onlyFileReports)`. Change-log entries are not messages, so a conversation that holds only external changes still counts as empty, and `body()` returns `AgentNotConfiguredPane` (line 581) in place of the thread. After a successful Connect, the "Connected" screen promises "Review its progress and results in this panel". For an external-only person, that promise is false.

**2. `workspace_unavailable` is used for ordinary refusals that the server instructions describe as "JusPrin is closed" (verified twice).** The server instructions say: "A workspace_unavailable error means you should open JusPrin and a project." `McpProtocol.cpp` `activity_result()` (line 261) maps every native `unavailable_operation` to `workspace_unavailable`. Two calls in this run came back with that code:
  - `slice_start` while a slice is running returned "A slice is already running. Wait for it, or ask again with preempt." (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:2141`).
  - `export_file` of an unsliced plate returned "Slice the plate first; it has no current G-code" (`OrcaOutputs.cpp:331`).

The message text is right, but a model that follows the code and the instructions will tell the person to open JusPrin. These need their own codes, or the instructions need to stop treating the code as meaning "closed".

**3. The same mistake gets different error codes in different tools (verified).**
  - A wrong `plateId` produces three different answers:
    - `slice_report` returns `invalid_arguments`, "The tool arguments do not match the registered contract.", with no details.
    - `slice_start` returns `invalid_id`, "No such plate".
    - `view_render` returns `stale_workspace`, "That plate is not in the open project", with `expectedRevision` equal to `currentRevision` (22 and 22), so the error claims the workspace changed when it did not. This comes from `WorkspaceError::StaleId` in `OrcaOutputs.cpp:151/328/338` and `OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:1556/1568/1573/2553/2604`, mapped in `McpProtocol.cpp` `activity_result()`.
  - `invalid_argument` (singular: import, export, attachment and cancel tools) sits beside `invalid_arguments` (plural: the decoder).
  - A wrong argument type (`objectId: 59`) returns the contract message with no field name, while a missing field does name it ("Missing: include").
  - `missing_object` from `object_analyze` and `object_place` has empty `details` and does not point to `workspace_inspect`. The object-scope `settings_get` does.

**4. The default `workspace_inspect` summary drops objects that are on no plate (verified).** I moved one of 41 objects to x = 600 mm. The summary then said `objectCount: 40`, the per-plate lists added up to 40, and the object appeared nowhere. The `objects` section still listed all 41, with `plateIds: []` for the moved one. `ToolResults.cpp` `workspace_inspection()` (around line 761) counts `plate.objects` instead of model objects. To a client reading the default view, the object looks deleted. The same sum would count an object twice if its copies sit on two plates; I did not test that case.

**5. "Connect" for Claude Code fails if JusPrin was ever connected before (verified with the real CLI).** Running the same `claude mcp add --scope user … jusprin` a second time exits 1 with "MCP server jusprin already exists in user config". The Connect screen would then show the generic "The setup command failed." This blocks reconnecting after the app moves, after a reinstall, or after a data folder change, and the old entry stays pointed at the old path. With a moved app path, `claude mcp list` shows "✘ Failed to connect — ENOENT … posix_spawn". `codex mcp add` overwrites instead, and so does the JSON-file path for Claude Desktop, Cursor and VS Code. Location: the `claude` arguments in `McpConnections.hpp` `connection_entries()`, and `AgentHost::handle_mcp_connect()`. One fix would be to remove the old entry before adding, after the person confirms.

**6. The race-loss message tells the client to repeat a call that cannot succeed (verified).** The losing side of the two-client race got "The project changed before this action could execute. Call the tool again." (`ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:942`). Repeating the apply with the same `expectedRevision` will fail again. The correct next step, which the other `stale_workspace` message gives, is to read and preview again.

**7. The server instructions are thin and partly wrong (verified against the catalog).**
  - They cover only the settings workflow.
  - They say "use preset revert", but no preset-revert tool exists among the 27.
  - They say nothing about polling slices, ids being scoped to a session, or `workspace_inspect` being the entry point.

Location: `McpProtocol.cpp` `discovery()` at line 178. The bridge copies the same text into `initialize`.

# JusPrin MCP experience: findings (2026-10-21)

Working note, untracked. Do not commit.

## 1. Problem

JusPrin runs an MCP server inside the app so that external AI tools (Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code) can drive the open project. External clients start a small stdio program, `jusprin-mcp` (the "bridge"), which forwards their calls to the app. The question was: when a real client uses this the way the setup screen tells a person to, does it work, can a model pick the right tool from the descriptions alone, do errors say what to call next, are results a sensible size, and does the app show the person what the external tool did?

Short answer: the core workflow works end to end, and most errors are good. The two biggest gaps are about the person rather than the protocol. First, a person who uses only an external tool sees nothing in the Agent panel about what that tool changed. Second, the error code `workspace_unavailable` is used for ordinary situations like "a slice is already running", while the server's own instructions tell the model that this code means "open JusPrin and a project". Everything else is smaller: inconsistent error codes, one counting bug, and one setup command that fails the second time.

## 2. What was tested and how

- **Build.** I used the existing `build/arm64/src/RelWithDebInfo/OrcaSlicer.app`, built at 04:16 today while HEAD was 05a044f707, which is the commit the gap review covered. Commits since then (f073fdba96) do not touch `Mcp/`, `ToolRegistry.cpp` or the workspace adapter. I copied the bundle to my scratchpad, gave the copy its own bundle id (`com.jusprin.mcp-experience-test`), and ad-hoc signed it, so the build could not overwrite it and screenshots could not bind to another JusPrin instance. A fresh RelWithDebInfo rebuild (919 steps) was too slow at load average 21 to 32. Another session was also building Release in the same build folder, so I stopped my build at step 253. The app binary used here is therefore from the reviewed commit, not today's HEAD.
- **Isolation.** The app ran as `OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch>/data <model>`, with `HOME=<scratch>/home`. Its config was `tests/data/jusprin/harness.conf` (stealth mode, version check pointed at a closed port, single instance off). The MCP server took port 47301. Kenneth's own data folder had no discovery file, so the ~75 `jusprin-mcp` processes belonging to other Claude sessions on this machine kept answering offline and never reached this instance. For the "agent configured" run, the config held a fake OpenAI key and the app ran with `JUSPRIN_AGENT_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:1/v1`, so no model could be called or billed.
- **Client.** I wrote a scripted stdio MCP client (`mcpclient.py` in my scratchpad). It starts the bundled `jusprin-mcp --discovery <data>/jusprin/mcp.json` exactly as the Connect screen writes it into a client config, negotiates protocol `2025-06-18` as Claude Code does, and logs every exchange with its size and latency (388 calls). No paid model was used. The real Claude Code CLI was used only for `claude mcp add`, `mcp list` and `mcp get`, which make no model calls.
- **Covered:** initialize and version negotiation; `tools/list` with paging; offline behaviour; `workspace_inspect` (every section); `object_analyze`; `settings_search`, `settings_get`, `settings_preview_patch` and `settings_apply_patch`; `slice_start`, `slice_report`, `slice_inspect`, `view_render`; `object_place` (rotate, position, autoOrient); `plate_layout` (quantity, arrange); `object_import_file`; `project_open` (new, STL, 3MF, the opened-before flow); `export_file`; `project_delete_items`; `presets_list`; `printer_setup_preview`; `printer_list`; `project_attachment_read`; `activity_cancel`.
- **Error paths covered:** a stale revision, a wrong session, unknown object, plate and setting ids, a bad enum value, a value out of range, blocked and withheld keys, wrong argument types, an extra field, an unknown tool, and a feature handle that has expired.
- **Lifecycle:** cancelling a slice, slicing while a slice is running, `preempt`, re-slicing an unchanged plate, a client cancelling its request, the client closing mid-call, two clients racing, calls made while a modal dialog is open, 40 objects, and an app quit and relaunch under a live client.
- **Screenshots** of the test app with and without an in-app agent configured.
- **Existing suites:** `JUSPRIN_TEST_BRIDGE=<copy>/jusprin-mcp python3 -m unittest discover -s tests/mcp` gave **18 tests, OK (1 skipped)**. `agent_bridge_tests "[mcp],[mcp_setup],[bridge]"` gave **All tests passed (894 assertions in 57 test cases)**, but that binary dates from 2026-10-20 19:30, before 05a044f707, which also changed `tests/agent`.

### What works (verified)

- **Setup commands work the first time.** `claude mcp add --scope user --transport stdio jusprin -- <bridge> --discovery <data>/jusprin/mcp.json` printed "Added stdio MCP server jusprin". `claude mcp get jusprin` then printed `Status: ✔ Connected`.

- **Version negotiation.** A client asking for `2025-03-26`, `2025-06-18` or `2025-11-25` gets that version. A client asking for `2024-11-05` is answered with `2025-06-18`.
- **Catalog.** There are 27 tools. The first page holds 25 (34,291 bytes on the wire) and the second page holds `view_render` and `workspace_inspect` (2,593 bytes). The descriptions are detailed and say which call comes next, for example "Preview first", "read from workspace_inspect's slicing section", and "Handles are valid until the project changes".
- **Settings workflow.** Preview of `{"wall_loops":4,"sparse_infill_density":"25%"}` returned before/after values and `valid: true`. Unknown keys come back with suggestions (`wall_loop` suggests `wall_loops`; `infil_density` suggests `sparse_infill_density`). A bad enum lists all 26 allowed values. Out of range gives `min`/`max`. # JusPrin MCP experience: findings (2026-10-21)

Working note, untracked. Do not commit.

## 1. Problem

JusPrin runs an MCP server inside the app so that external AI tools (Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code) can drive the open project. External clients start a small stdio program, `jusprin-mcp` (the "bridge"), which forwards their calls to the app. The question was: when a real client uses this the way the setup screen tells a person to, does it work, can a model pick the right tool from the descriptions alone, do errors say what to call next, are results a sensible size, and does the app show the person what the external tool did?

Short answer: the core workflow works end to end, and most errors are good. The two biggest gaps are about the person rather than the protocol. First, a person who uses only an external tool sees nothing in the Agent panel about what that tool changed. Second, the error code `workspace_unavailable` is used for ordinary situations like "a slice is already running", while the server's own instructions tell the model that this code means "open JusPrin and a project". Everything else is smaller: inconsistent error codes, one counting bug, and one setup command that fails the second time.

## 2. What was tested and how

- **Build.** I used the existing `build/arm64/src/RelWithDebInfo/OrcaSlicer.app`, built at 04:16 today while HEAD was 05a044f707, which is the commit the gap review covered. Commits since then (f073fdba96) do not touch `Mcp/`, `ToolRegistry.cpp` or the workspace adapter. I copied the bundle to my scratchpad, gave the copy its own bundle id (`com.jusprin.mcp-experience-test`), and ad-hoc signed it, so the build could not overwrite it and screenshots could not bind to another JusPrin instance. A fresh RelWithDebInfo rebuild (919 steps) was too slow at load average 21 to 32. Another session was also building Release in the same build folder, so I stopped my build at step 253. The app binary used here is therefore from the reviewed commit, not today's HEAD.
- **Isolation.** The app ran as `OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch>/data <model>`, with `HOME=<scratch>/home`. Its config was `tests/data/jusprin/harness.conf` (stealth mode, version check pointed at a closed port, single instance off). The MCP server took port 47301. Kenneth's own data folder had no discovery file, so the ~75 `jusprin-mcp` processes belonging to other Claude sessions on this machine kept answering offline and never reached this instance. For the "agent configured" run, the config held a fake OpenAI key and the app ran with `JUSPRIN_AGENT_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:1/v1`, so no model could be called or billed.
- **Client.** I wrote a scripted stdio MCP client (`mcpclient.py` in my scratchpad). It starts the bundled `jusprin-mcp --discovery <data>/jusprin/mcp.json` exactly as the Connect screen writes it into a client config, negotiates protocol `2025-06-18` as Claude Code does, and logs every exchange with its size and latency (388 calls). No paid model was used. The real Claude Code CLI was used only for `claude mcp add`, `mcp list` and `mcp get`, which make no model calls.
- **Covered:** initialize and version negotiation; `tools/list` with paging; offline behaviour; `workspace_inspect` (every section); `object_analyze`; `settings_search`, `settings_get`, `settings_preview_patch` and `settings_apply_patch`; `slice_start`, `slice_report`, `slice_inspect`, `view_render`; `object_place` (rotate, position, autoOrient); `plate_layout` (quantity, arrange); `object_import_file`; `project_open` (new, STL, 3MF, the opened-before flow); `export_file`; `project_delete_items`; `presets_list`; `printer_setup_preview`; `printer_list`; `project_attachment_read`; `activity_cancel`.
- **Error paths covered:** a stale revision, a wrong session, unknown object, plate and setting ids, a bad enum value, a value out of range, blocked and withheld keys, wrong argument types, an extra field, an unknown tool, and a feature handle that has expired.
- **Lifecycle:** cancelling a slice, slicing while a slice is running, `preempt`, re-slicing an unchanged plate, a client cancelling its request, the client closing mid-call, two clients racing, calls made while a modal dialog is open, 40 objects, and an app quit and relaunch under a live client.
- **Screenshots** of the test app with and without an in-app agent configured.
- **Existing suites:** `JUSPRIN_TEST_BRIDGE=<copy>/jusprin-mcp python3 -m unittest discover -s tests/mcp` gave **18 tests, OK (1 skipped)**. `agent_bridge_tests "[mcp],[mcp_setup],[bridge]"` gave **All tests passed (894 assertions in 57 test cases)**, but that binary dates from 2026-10-20 19:30, before 05a044f707, which also changed `tests/agent`.

## 3. Results

### What works (verified)

- **Setup commands work the first time.** `claude mcp add --scope user --transport stdio jusprin -- <bridge> --discovery <data>/jusprin/mcp.json` printed "Added stdio MCP server jusprin". `claude mcp get jusprin` then printed `Status: ✔ Connected`.
- **Offline behaviour is clear.** With the app closed, `initialize` and `tools/list` still answer from the bridge's built-in catalog. A tool call returns `workspace_unavailable`: "Open JusPrin and a project, then try again. The bridge does not launch JusPrin."
- **Version negotiation.** A client asking for `2025-03-26`, `2025-06-18` or `2025-11-25` gets that version. A client asking for `2024-11-05` is answered with `2025-06-18`.
- **Catalog.** There are 27 tools. The first page holds 25 (34,291 bytes on the wire) and the second page holds `view_render` and `workspace_inspect` (2,593 bytes). The descriptions are detailed and say which call comes next, for example "Preview first", "read from workspace_inspect's slicing section", and "Handles are valid until the project changes".
- **Settings workflow.** Preview of `{"wall_loops":4,"sparse_infill_density":"25%"}` returned before/after values and `valid: true`. Apply returned `applied: true` and moved the revision from 7 to 8. `settings_get` then showed `differsFromPreset: true`. Unknown keys come back with suggestions (`wall_loop` suggests `wall_loops`; `infil_density` suggests `sparse_infill_density`). A bad enum lists all 26 allowed values. Out of range gives `min`/`max`. Withheld keys (`print_host`) return a clear message saying the person changes it in the printer's connection settings.
- **Slicing.**
  - `slice_start` returns a handle immediately with a note that the client must poll. Slicing finished after about 30 s (111 s for three copies at load average 30).
  - `slice_report` (2.6 KB for all eight sections) gave time, grams, cost and Orca's own warning text.
  - `activity_cancel` stopped a running slice (`"cancelled": true`). A second `slice_start` with `preempt` replaced a running slice. Re-slicing an unchanged plate returned `alreadySliced: true` immediately. This means the hang recorded on 2026-10-15 (memory "manual-mcp-tool-repro-recipe", trap 2) no longer happens.
- **Images.** `view_render` returned a 1024×768 PNG of 12,394 bytes as an MCP image block. It looked correct.
- **Stale handling.** Two clients previewed at the same revision and applied at the same time. The first applied. The second got `stale_workspace` with the expected and current revision, and nothing was changed twice. An expired face handle gives `feature_expired` with "Read the features again".
- **`project_open`.** The opened-before flow returns a clear question for the person ("Ask the person whether to continue that project or start a new one…"). Orca's own dialogs are answered and reported, for example "The 3MF is not supported by JusPrin, loading geometry data only."
- **Lifecycle.**
  - A `notifications/cancelled` sent before the call started meant the project was not opened.
  - When the client closed its input 0.3 s into `project_open`, the bridge exited in 0.01 s and the open still completed. This matches the documented "outcome unknown" behaviour.
  - With the Preferences dialog open, reads and a settings apply all completed and nothing hung.
  - The same bridge process followed the app through a quit and relaunch.
- **With an in-app agent configured, the panel shows external work.** It showed "Wall loops 2 → 3 · External tool, in 0.20mm Standard @BBL X1C", "Place object · External tool", a "Slicing plate 1" card with Cancel, and a "1 print issue" chip.

### Shortcomings, ranked

**1. A person who uses only an external tool cannot see what it changed (verified).** No in-app agent was configured. Through MCP I changed wall loops from 2 to 3, rotated the object, and started a slice. The Agent panel kept showing "NOT SET UP" and "No agent connected", plus a header card that read "Preset fallback · 0.20mm Standard @BBL X1C · No agent configured · using the selected preset". That card is wrong: the preset had unsaved edits from the external tool. The edits are recorded. The project's `current-state.json` holds `changes` entries with `"external": true`, `"from": "2"`, `"to": "3"`. The panel never shows them. The cause is `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/App.tsx`, line 421: `notConfigured = unavailable && (… || onlyFileReports)`. Change-log entries are not messages, so a conversation that holds only external changes still counts as empty, and `body()` returns `AgentNotConfiguredPane` (line 581) in place of the thread. After a successful Connect, the "Connected" screen promises "Review its progress and results in this panel". For an external-only person, that promise is false.

**2. `workspace_unavailable` is used for ordinary refusals that the server instructions describe as "JusPrin is closed" (verified twice).** The server instructions say: "A workspace_unavailable error means you should open JusPrin and a project." `McpProtocol.cpp` `activity_result()` (line 261) maps every native `unavailable_operation` to `workspace_unavailable`. Two calls in this run came back with that code:
  - `slice_start` while a slice is running returned "A slice is already running. Wait for it, or ask again with preempt." (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:2141`).
  - `export_file` of an unsliced plate returned "Slice the plate first; it has no current G-code" (`OrcaOutputs.cpp:331`).

The message text is right, but a model that follows the code and the instructions will tell the person to open JusPrin. These need their own codes, or the instructions need to stop treating the code as meaning "closed".

**3. The same mistake gets different error codes in different tools (verified).**
  - A wrong `plateId` produces three different answers:
    - `slice_report` returns `invalid_arguments`, "The tool arguments do not match the registered contract.", with no details.
    - `slice_start` returns `invalid_id`, "No such plate".
    - `view_render` returns `stale_workspace`, "That plate is not in the open project", with `expectedRevision` equal to `currentRevision` (22 and 22), so the error claims the workspace changed when it did not. This comes from `WorkspaceError::StaleId` in `OrcaOutputs.cpp:151/328/338` and `OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:1556/1568/1573/2553/2604`, mapped in `McpProtocol.cpp` `activity_result()`.
  - `invalid_argument` (singular: import, export, attachment and cancel tools) sits beside `invalid_arguments` (plural: the decoder).
  - A wrong argument type (`objectId: 59`) returns the contract message with no field name, while a missing field does name it ("Missing: include").
  - `missing_object` from `object_analyze` and `object_place` has empty `details` and does not point to `workspace_inspect`. The object-scope `settings_get` does.

**4. The default `workspace_inspect` summary drops objects that are on no plate (verified).** I moved one of 41 objects to x = 600 mm. The summary then said `objectCount: 40`, the per-plate lists added up to 40, and the object appeared nowhere. The `objects` section still listed all 41, with `plateIds: []` for the moved one. `ToolResults.cpp` `workspace_inspection()` (around line 761) counts `plate.objects` instead of model objects. To a client reading the default view, the object looks deleted. The same sum would count an object twice if its copies sit on two plates; I did not test that case.

**5. "Connect" for Claude Code fails if JusPrin was ever connected before (verified with the real CLI).** Running the same `claude mcp add --scope user … jusprin` a second time exits 1 with "MCP server jusprin already exists in user config". The Connect screen would then show the generic "The setup command failed." This blocks reconnecting after the app moves, after a reinstall, or after a data folder change, and the old entry stays pointed at the old path. With a moved app path, `claude mcp list` shows "✘ Failed to connect — ENOENT … posix_spawn". `codex mcp add` overwrites instead, and so does the JSON-file path for Claude Desktop, Cursor and VS Code. Location: the `claude` arguments in `McpConnections.hpp` `connection_entries()`, and `AgentHost::handle_mcp_connect()`. One fix would be to remove the old entry before adding, after the person confirms.

**6. The race-loss message tells the client to repeat a call that cannot succeed (verified).** The losing side of the two-client race got "The project changed before this action could execute. Call the tool again." (`ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:942`). Repeating the apply with the same `expectedRevision` will fail again. The correct next step, which the other `stale_workspace` message gives, is to read and preview again.

**7. The server instructions are thin and partly wrong (verified against the catalog).**
  - They cover only the settings workflow.
  - They say "use preset revert", but no preset-revert tool exists among the 27.
  - They say nothing about polling slices, ids being scoped to a session, or `workspace_inspect` being the entry point.

Location: `McpProtocol.cpp` `discovery()` at line 178. The bridge copies the same text into `initialize`.

**8. `settings_apply_patch` promises a binding to the preview that it does not enforce (verified).** Its description says it "Requires the sessionId and revision from a preview of the same scope, target, changes and persistAs". Applying `{"wall_loops": 6}`, which was never previewed, with a current revision succeeded (`applied: true`, revision 21 to 22). So did `{"layer_height": 0.16}` sent with the revision from a preview of `wall_loops: 5`. This is safe, because the app previews again internally ("Apply binds the previewed values" in the tool guide). The description overstates the contract, though, and a client cannot rely on "apply only what I showed the person". Location: the `settings_apply_patch` entry in `ToolRegistry.cpp` at line 1062.

**9. Printers that are not installed are out of reach, and the error does not say so (verified).** In a data folder with only the X1C installed, `presets_list {kind: printer, query: "mk4", compatibleOnly: false}` returned 0 results. `printer_setup_preview {printerPreset: "Prusa MK4"}` said "No installed printer preset is named "Prusa MK4". Read presets_list." Reading `presets_list` cannot help. The message should tell the model to ask the person to add the printer in JusPrin (Home → Add printer). Location: `OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:1272`.

**10. Smaller issues (verified unless marked).**
  - **Search ranking.** `settings_search "wall loops"` ranks `tree_support_wall_count` first and `wall_loops`, the exact key, third.
  - **Blocked keys.** `post_process` and `print_host` are refused with "This process setting is read-only." (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:3198`). The message gives no reason and no route, unlike `withheld_setting`.
  - **Empty plate.** `slice_start` refuses with only "OrcaSlicer did not start slicing this plate." (`ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:1791`). It does not say the plate is empty.
  - **`activity_cancel` on a finished slice** says "That slice has ended; a slice started since is not the tools' to stop." This is confusing when no other slice was started.
  - **`history.canRedo` is `true`** right after every fresh load and `project_open new`. The value comes from `Plater::can_redo_project()`. I did not check whether Orca's Edit → Redo is enabled at the same moment, so this is unexplained, not proven wrong.
  - **Startup window.** While the app is still loading a model given on the command line, the MCP server already answers with an empty "Untitled" project. The model then arrives in the same `sessionId` with a higher revision. Seen once.
  - **Latency.** The first `slice_start` of the session took 21.4 s to return. The other ten took 0.03 to 0.97 s. The machine was at load average around 30, so this is a single observation.

**11. Possible size problems (not verified with a real client).**
  - `slice_inspect {view: gcode}` returns up to 64 KB of G-code, and the result carries it twice, as the text block and as `structuredContent`. That came to 139,545 bytes on the wire. Third-party pages (not official docs) say Claude Code caps an MCP result at 25,000 tokens by default and warns at 10,000. Sources: [xpoz help](https://help.xpoz.ai/en/articles/12681842-claude-code-mcp-tool-exceeds-maximum-allowed-tokens-25000), [nuilab reference](https://agenticai.nuilab.org/reference/token-and-thinking-limits/), [Figma MCP client issues](https://developers.figma.com/docs/figma-mcp-server/mcp-clients-issues). A full G-code page is probably near or over that cap. A smaller default page would avoid the risk.
  - The full catalog is about 37 KB on every turn for clients that load all tools.
  - Paging puts `workspace_inspect`, the entry tool, on page 2. Claude Code follows `nextCursor`: this session's own deferred list of `mcp__jusprin__*` tools includes both page-2 tools. Clients that do not follow `nextCursor` would never see `workspace_inspect`. I did not check other clients.

## 4. Remaining issues: what I could not test

- **No real model chose tools.** I did not run Claude Code, Codex or Claude Desktop with a model, because of the paid-run rule. So "are the descriptions enough to pick the right tool" is judged by reading them, not measured.
- **Claude Desktop, Cowork, Cursor and VS Code** were not launched. Their JSON entries are the same `command` + `args` that worked here.
- **The Connect button itself** was not clicked. I ran the exact CLI commands it builds. The review-diff screen for the JSON-file clients was not exercised.
- **Downloaded app.** macOS App Translocation and quarantine of a downloaded app: if the bridge path recorded by Connect is a translocated path, every entry would break on the next launch. Not tested.
- **Other platforms.** Windows and Linux were not tested.
- **Harness modes.** The shell harness modes (`--mcp`, `--mcp-bridge`, `--mcp-setup`) were not run, because the harness binary is from 2026-10-20 and I stopped the rebuild.
- **Old test binary.** `agent_bridge_tests` ran from an older binary, as noted in section 2.
- **Product questions, not defects.** Geometry tools (`object_place`, `plate_layout`) check only `sessionId`, not a revision. An external call can therefore silently overwrite a move the person just made in the GUI. Mutations also run while the person is inside a modal dialog. I did not treat either as a defect.

Evidence lives in my scratchpad (`/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/61322f1f-4e98-48dc-a835-8cd76da05f22/scratchpad`). It holds `transcript.jsonl` with all 388 calls, `catalog.json`, `render_iso.png`, the test scripts, and the isolated data folder. The test app is shut down. Nothing in the repository was changed apart from this file.

# JusPrin production documentation

This directory is the canonical starting point for production work on `jusprin-newui`. It preserves the durable product and engineering decisions from `jusprin-v2-poc` without importing the POC's temporary windows, probes, static mocks, generated evidence, or environment-gated startup paths.

Read these documents in order:

1. [Product definition](product-definition.md) — the human/agent boundary, required product surfaces, workflow, and visibility rules.
2. [Production architecture](architecture.md) — the selected native/WebView architecture, ownership rules, component boundaries, and implementation sequence.
3. [Engineering and verification method](engineering-method.md) — how to assess risk and what evidence is required before calling a feature complete.
4. [OrcaSlicer integration guide](orca-integration-guide.md) — known Orca behaviors, lifecycle traps, event and history constraints, and testing lessons.
5. [Fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md) — required before changing any OrcaSlicer-owned file: where a seam belongs, why additive beats rewritten, how to leave a conflict that resolves correctly, and what evidence a change must record.
6. [Design system](design-system.md) — brand behavior, semantic UI tokens, typography, spacing, accessibility, and asset rules.
7. [POC reference](poc-reference.md) — exact pointers to the spike-only documents, code, commits, logs, screenshots, and generated brand artifacts left on `jusprin-v2-poc`.
8. [Tool extension guide](mcp-tool-extension-guide.md) — shared Agent/MCP contracts, process-settings workflow, execution and verification requirements.
9. [Local autosave and version history](autosave-version-history.md) — managed project storage, migration, restore, export, retention, and failure behavior.

Printer UI without hardware (Bambu in-process fake; control file; isolated app): [Fake Bambu README](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md). Print-host (Klipper/Moonraker) simulation stays on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter`.

## Governing decisions

- JusPrin is an AI-piloted 3D-printing product built on OrcaSlicer, not a replacement slicing engine.
- OrcaSlicer's C++ model, slicing pipeline, viewport, geometry operations, project serialization, and undo stack remain authoritative.
- The production application stays native C++/wxWidgets/OpenGL. The Agent conversation uses a local React/TypeScript application inside `wxWebView`.
- JavaScript renders state and submits typed commands; it never owns editable Orca project state.
- When logic could live in either C++ or a React page, it goes in the page unless there is a strong reason for C++: it touches Orca state, enforces a limit or boundary the app must guarantee, has to work without a page, or needs a thread or lifetime the page lacks. See [Where logic goes](architecture.md#where-logic-goes-the-page-first).
- Product policy lives in fork-owned files. OrcaSlicer-owned files receive only small, product-neutral, additive seams — every line changed there is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase.
- The user owns physical facts, object meaning, desired outcomes, privacy and legal decisions, and starting consequential physical actions.
- The production branch must not import experimental POC behavior merely because it demonstrated feasibility. Use the POC as evidence and reimplement through stable production boundaries.

## Source lineage

`jusprin-newui` and `jusprin-v2-poc` share base commit `8500fcdcca` (`v2.4.2`). The POC reference is pinned to final POC commit `9bba835b92`, so future changes to branch names do not make the historical evidence ambiguous.
61:| Agent conversation | React/TypeScript WebView | Render messages, write the words people and the model read, and submit typed commands (see [Where logic goes](#where-logic-goes-the-page-first)) |
62:| Agent print plan | C++/agent application boundary | Explain intent, decisions, uncertainty, and consequences |
63:
64:## Production integration boundaries
65:
66:### Shell host
67:
68:The shell is the JusPrin window frame around OrcaSlicer's content. Build one shell, in files this fork owns, and attach it to `MainFrame` in one small place. Decisions about what happens at startup go in a bootstrap or a shell factory that the fork owns. Do not spread environment checks through OrcaSlicer's constructors.
69:
70:The first production version may still construct OrcaSlicer's old top bar, tab panel, Sidebar, and `GUI_ObjectList` where existing OrcaSlicer behavior depends on them. Leave them out of the visible layout. Do not hide them behind a separate top-level window. Stopping them from being constructed at all is a separate project, because it changes object lifetimes.
71:
72:### Build registration
73:
74:List JusPrin's source files explicitly in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/sources.cmake`. OrcaSlicer's central `src/slic3r/CMakeLists.txt` should pull that file in with one include line that never changes. The fork should not keep adding its own files to OrcaSlicer's list.
75:
76:### Workspace boundary
77:
78:The workspace API is the typed C++ interface JusPrin uses to read and change the project. The production version should keep the ideas from the proof of concept (POC) that worked:
79:
80:- separate types for plate IDs and object IDs, so one cannot be passed where the other is expected;
81:- read-only snapshots of the project;
82:- explicit errors from commands;
83:- typed reasons that say what kind of change happened;
84:- a revision number that only goes up;
85:- subscriptions that end automatically when the object holding them is destroyed, and that can be moved but not copied.
86:
87:Before production use, the API must also:
88:
89:- say which calls must run on the GUI thread;
90:- say exactly when the revision number goes up;
91:- explicitly mark the old session's IDs invalid when a project is replaced;
92:- notice changes that did not go through the adapter (the JusPrin class that implements this API on top of OrcaSlicer);
93:- report undo and redo availability whether or not any particular widget is visible;
94:- report whether an undo or redo really changed OrcaSlicer's state;
95:- not depend on `GUI_ObjectList` for commands that change the model;
96:- offer plate selection, object import and addition, and the other commands the product needs;
97:- keep wxWidgets types and OrcaSlicer types out of its public interface.
98:
99:Sometimes the operation you need exists only inside OrcaSlicer's UI code. In that case, add the smallest possible command to the OrcaSlicer class that already does the work, and name it for what it does. Do not copy the operation into JusPrin. Do not fake clicks or key presses on hidden controls.
100:
101:### Canvas presentation
--
166:#### Where logic goes: the page first
167:
168:When the same logic could live either in C++ or in a React page, put it in the page unless there is a strong reason for C++. The page is quicker to change: Vite hot-reloads it, while a C++ change means relinking a multi-gigabyte GUI library. The page's tests run in milliseconds under Vitest. The text people read is already written in the page. The text the model reads belongs there too.
169:
170:Strong reasons for C++:
171:
172:- **It reads or changes OrcaSlicer state:** presets, the model, plates, slicing, the device list. The page never owns project state (see the constraints below).
173:- **The app has to guarantee it.** This covers what a tool accepts and refuses, which tools a session may call, and what is sent to the model provider (API keys, access codes, project data). Page code can describe a limit, but only the app can enforce one.
174:- **It has to work without a page:** the MCP server, background work, tests that run without a browser.
175:- **It needs a thread the page does not have, or has to stay alive at times when the page is not.**
176:
177:The printer panel shows how this works. The app sends the page only facts: sizes, spools, which printer a card shows, and what a change altered. The page turns those facts into all of the text:
178:
179:- The page writes the model's instructions in `AgentUI/src/printerInstructions.ts` and sends them to the app with `printer_instructions`.
180:- The page writes the panel's own text in `AgentUI/src/printerWords.ts`. That is the opening line and the note that goes with each tap. The opening line is sent with `printer_opening`. The note for a tap is sent inside that tap's payload.
181:
182:The app's part:
183:

- The production branch must not import experimental POC behavior merely because it demonstrated feasibility. Use the POC as evidence and reimplement through stable production boundaries.

## Source lineage

`jusprin-newui` and `jusprin-v2-poc` share base commit `8500fcdcca` (`v2.4.2`). The POC reference is pinned to final POC commit `9bba835b92`, so future changes to branch names do not make the historical evidence ambiguous.

64:## Production integration boundaries
65:
66:### Shell host
67:
68:The shell is the JusPrin window frame around OrcaSlicer's content. Build one shell, in files this fork owns, and attach it to `MainFrame` in one small place. Decisions about what happens at startup go in a bootstrap or a shell factory that the fork owns. Do not spread environment checks through OrcaSlicer's constructors.
69:
70:The first production version may still construct OrcaSlicer's old top bar, tab panel, Sidebar, and `GUI_ObjectList` where existing OrcaSlicer behavior depends on them. Leave them out of the visible layout. Do not hide them behind a separate top-level window. Stopping them from being constructed at all is a separate project, because it changes object lifetimes.
71:
72:### Build registration
73:
74:List JusPrin's source files explicitly in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/sources.cmake`. OrcaSlicer's central `src/slic3r/CMakeLists.txt` should pull that file in with one include line that never changes. The fork should not keep adding its own files to OrcaSlicer's list.
75:
76:### Workspace boundary
77:
78:The workspace API is the typed C++ interface JusPrin uses to read and change the project. The production version should keep the ideas from the proof of concept (POC) that worked:
79:
80:- separate types for plate IDs and object IDs, so one cannot be passed where the other is expected;
81:- read-only snapshots of the project;
82:- explicit errors from commands;
83:- typed reasons that say what kind of change happened;
84:- a revision number that only goes up;
85:- subscriptions that end automatically when the object holding them is destroyed, and that can be moved but not copied.
86:
87:Before production use, the API must also:
88:
89:- say which calls must run on the GUI thread;
90:- say exactly when the revision number goes up;
91:- explicitly mark the old session's IDs invalid when a project is replaced;
92:- notice changes that did not go through the adapter (the JusPrin class that implements this API on top of OrcaSlicer);
93:- report undo and redo availability whether or not any particular widget is visible;
94:- report whether an undo or redo really changed OrcaSlicer's state;
95:- not depend on `GUI_ObjectList` for commands that change the model;
96:- offer plate selection, object import and addition, and the other commands the product needs;
97:- keep wxWidgets types and OrcaSlicer types out of its public interface.
98:
99:Sometimes the operation you need exists only inside OrcaSlicer's UI code. In that case, add the smallest possible command to the OrcaSlicer class that already does the work, and name it for what it does. Do not copy the operation into JusPrin. Do not fake clicks or key presses on hidden controls.

166:#### Where logic goes: the page first
167:
168:When the same logic could live either in C++ or in a React page, put it in the page unless there is a strong reason for C++. The page is quicker to change: Vite hot-reloads it, while a C++ change means relinking a multi-gigabyte GUI library. The page's tests run in milliseconds under Vitest. The text people read is already written in the page. The text the model reads belongs there too.
169:
170:Strong reasons for C++:
171:
172:- **It reads or changes OrcaSlicer state:** presets, the model, plates, slicing, the device list. The page never owns project state (see the constraints below).
173:- **The app has to guarantee it.** This covers what a tool accepts and refuses, which tools a session may call, and what is sent to the model provider (API keys, access codes, project data). Page code can describe a limit, but only the app can enforce one.
174:- **It has to work without a page:** the MCP server, background work, tests that run without a browser.
175:- **It needs a thread the page does not have, or has to stay alive at times when the page is not.**
176:
177:The printer panel shows how this works. The app sends the page only facts: sizes, spools, which printer a card shows, and what a change altered. The page turns those facts into all of the text:

180:- The page writes the panel's own text in `AgentUI/src/printerWords.ts`. That is the opening line and the note that goes with each tap. The opening line is sent with `printer_opening`. The note for a tap is sent inside that tap's payload.
