# Composer

The message box at the bottom of the Agent pane, following common AI chat apps: staged files, a text area that grows with the message, and a toolbar to attach, choose the model and thinking level, and send.

- You supply `value`, `onChange`, `onSend`, `onAttach(type)` and optionally `state` (`idle`, `streaming` or `unavailable`), `mode` (`regular` or `photo`), `attachments` (the props of each staged `ChatAttachment`), `models` with `model` and `onModelChange`, `thinkingLevels` with `thinking` and `onThinkingChange`, `onStop` and `placeholder`.
- One box with `space-8` padding, `space-4` between its parts, `radius-medium` corners and a 1px `border-subtle` stroke, on `surface-canvas`. Staged files sit inside it above the text, `space-4` apart.
- The text area starts one line high in `body-small` and grows a line at a time up to `component-composer-maxLines` (8) lines, then the text scrolls inside it. Enter sends; Shift+Enter adds a line. The placeholder is `text-tertiary`.
- The toolbar: on the left a `ButtonIcon` with `plus`, then the model picker, then the thinking picker; on the right a compact `ButtonPrimary` labelled Send. A picker is `label` text and a `chevron-down`, `space-4` by `space-8` padding, `radius-small`; it fills with `surface-selected` while its menu is open.
- + opens a `MenuPopover` above it with four `MenuRow`s: Photo or image, 3D model (STL, 3MF, STEP), G-code, Document (PDF). Each opens the system file picker filtered to that type.
- When the pane is too narrow for both full labels beside + and Send, the thinking picker drops "Thinking:" and shows the level alone ("Medium"); if that still does not fit, the model name is cut with "…". + and Send keep their size.
- A model menu with more than 12 models starts with a `FieldSearch` ("Search models") above the provider groups, and opens with the cursor in it and the highlight on the chat's current model. Typing filters by model or provider name, ignoring case; providers with no match drop out, the first match is highlighted (Enter picks it, Up and Down move), and with no match the list reads "No models match “…”." Escape clears the search, a second Escape closes the menu. The list scrolls under the field. With 12 models or fewer there is no field. See the canvas board "model-menu-search · proposal".
- The model menu lists the models of every connected provider, each group under a `MenuSectionTitle` with the provider's name; with one provider the heading is left out. The thinking menu lists only the levels the chosen model supports, and the thinking picker is left out for a model without levels. Switching models keeps the level if the new model has it, otherwise it falls back to that model's default. Both choices apply to the current chat only.
- Send is disabled until there is text or a file; a file alone can be sent. While the Agent is replying the placeholder reads "Agent is responding…", Send becomes a Stop `ButtonSecondary`, and + and the pickers are disabled.
- Unavailable is different from empty: the box turns `surface-subtle`, the placeholder reads "Chat is unavailable" in `action-disabled-text`, and everything but the text is disabled.
- Photo mode (the printer chat, where only a photo can be attached) shows a "Photo" `ButtonLink` instead of + and has no pickers.
- Keyboard focus in the text draws a 2px `border-focus` stroke around the whole box.

# ButtonPrimary

The one decisive action in a view: the thing the screen is for. Use it once per view; every other action is a `ButtonSecondary`, a `ButtonIcon` or a `ButtonLink`.

- You supply the label as children and, optionally, `icon`: one 16px `Icon`.
- Label: verb first, sentence case, no full stop. "Slice plate", "Add printer", "Send to printer".
- Fill is `action-primary`, label `action-on-primary` in `body-small-bold`, corners `radius-medium`, padding `space-8` by `space-16`, so it stands 34px tall.
- Hover and pressed are `action-primary-hover` and `action-primary-pressed`. Disabled keeps the fill at 40% opacity; do not swap to a grey.
- Keyboard focus draws the 2px `border-focus` ring, offset 2px.
- Do not stretch it full width except in a narrow sheet, and do not place two side by side.

Both pages find their host through `window.wx.postMessage(json)` and receive host
envelopes through `window.__jusprinBridge.deliver(envelope)` (`WebShared/bridgeClient.ts`).
Copy `resources/jusprin/{agent,home}/index.html` to a scratch dir, inject
`<script>` right after `<head>` that (1) defines `window.wx` answering `hello` with
`hello_ack` + a full `state`, and (2) exposes `window.fake.deliver(type, payload)`;
serve with `python3 -m http.server` and open `agent.html?panel=printer` /
`home.html` via `preview_start`. Drive it with `javascript_tool`: deliver
`assistant_started` with no `assistant_delta` to freeze a streaming empty turn,
`printer_session` to pin a card, `printer_added` for Home's receipt strip. A file
drop works with `new DragEvent('drop', {dataTransfer})` on `.app--printer`.
Envelope: `{protocol:'jusprin-agent-bridge'|'jusprin-home-bridge', version:1, id, type, payload}`.
Used 2026-09-19 to review branch these-commits-are-probably-wrong in ~10 minutes.

**Why:** the desktop tools were locked by another session and background
`app_click` never reaches WKWebView content, so page-level states (streaming
activity line, compact photo chip, leave dialog, receipt strip) had no other cheap
proof. It proves page rendering only; host behaviour (e.g. the 256 KiB image
preview cap `kInlineImagePreviewCap` in `AgentHost.cpp`) must be replicated in
the fake by hand or checked live.

**How to apply:** reach for this before building a full app + datadir copy when the
question is "what does the page draw for state X". Pair with [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]]
for the host side. Related: [[render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof]].

14:add_executable(jusprin-mcp main.cpp)
"""Minimal stdio MCP client that drives jusprin-mcp the way Claude Code does.

Speaks protocol 2025-06-18 (what current Claude Code negotiates), newline-delimited
JSON-RPC over the bridge's stdin/stdout. Every exchange is appended to a JSONL
transcript with byte sizes so results can be quoted later.
"""
import json, os, queue, subprocess, sys, threading, time

S = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
BRIDGE = os.environ.get("BRIDGE", S + "/app/JusPrinTest.app/Contents/MacOS/jusprin-mcp")
DISCOVERY = os.environ.get("DISCOVERY", S + "/data/jusprin/mcp.json")
TRANSCRIPT = os.environ.get("TRANSCRIPT", S + "/transcript.jsonl")


class Client:
    def __init__(self, version="2025-06-18", args=None, env=None):
        cmd = [BRIDGE] + (args if args is not None else ["--discovery", DISCOVERY])
        self.p = subprocess.Popen(cmd, stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
                                  env={**os.environ, **(env or {})})
        self.q = queue.Queue()
        self.notes = []
        self.stderr = []
        threading.Thread(target=self._read, daemon=True).start()
        threading.Thread(target=lambda: [self.stderr.append(l.decode(errors="replace")) for l in self.p.stderr],
                         daemon=True).start()
        self.next_id = 1
        self.init = self.request("initialize", {"protocolVersion": version, "capabilities": {},
                                                "clientInfo": {"name": "mcp-experience-test", "version": "1"}})
        self.notify("notifications/initialized")

    def _read(self):
        for line in self.p.stdout:
            self.q.put((time.time(), line))

    def send(self, msg):
        self.p.stdin.write((json.dumps(msg) + "\n").encode())
        self.p.stdin.flush()

    def notify(self, method, params=None):
        self.send({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": method, "params": params or {}})

    def request(self, method, params=None, timeout=330, label=None, progress=False):
        i = self.next_id; self.next_id += 1
        params = dict(params or {})
        if progress:
            params["_meta"] = {"progressToken": "p%d" % i}
        t0 = time.time()
        self.send({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": i, "method": method, "params": params})
        while True:
            left = timeout - (time.time() - t0)
            if left <= 0:
                self._log(label or method, params, None, time.time() - t0, timeout=True)
                return None
            try:
                t, line = self.q.get(timeout=left)
            except queue.Empty:
                continue
            msg = json.loads(line)
            if msg.get("id") == i:
                self._log(label or method, params, msg, t - t0, size=len(line))

---
name: live-host-check-via-instrumented-dev-page
description: Test host behaviour in the real built app without screen control — point JUSPRIN_AGENT_DEV_URL at a copy of the built page with an injected script that logs envelopes to a local http.server and posts messages itself.
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 59133fd8-af56-4958-bb71-9b4812c085b8
  modified: 2026-10-21T14:27:05.386Z
---

2026-10-21 (saved-key work, branch claude/api-key-saved-state): Kenneth declined computer-use control of the app, and the Remove path's AppConfig code only runs in the real app. What worked in ~2 minutes:

1. Copy `resources/jusprin/agent/index.html` to a scratch dir, inject a `<script>` right after `<head>` that polls for `window.__jusprinBridge`, wraps its `deliver` to `fetch('http://127.0.0.1:<port>/log?'+JSON)` the envelopes of interest, and sends page messages with `window.wx.postMessage(JSON.stringify({protocol:'jusprin-agent-bridge',version:1,id,type,payload}))`.
2. Serve the dir with `python3 -m http.server <port> --bind 127.0.0.1 > server.log`; the request log is the test output.
3. Launch the built binary directly: `JUSPRIN_AGENT_DEV_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/page.html JUSPRIN_AGENT_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:9/v1 <app>/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with real *_api_key items deleted and TESTONLY keys added>`. The endpoint override keeps model-list and chat traffic off the real providers.
4. Read the data dir's JusPrin2.conf afterwards for persisted effects; delete the scratch data dir.

The fork's app bundle id is `io.jusprin.JusPrin` (not com.softfever3d.orca-slicer as [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] says). Related: [[fake-host-page-fixture]] (page-only states), [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

**Screenshots without screen control (2026-10-21):** add a `snap` command that POSTs `document.documentElement.outerHTML` (mark `document.activeElement` with `data-visual-focus` first) to a tiny local receiver, then strip `<script>`s, replace `:focus-visible` with `[data-visual-focus]`, pin `html,body` to the captured width (headless Chrome has a minimum window width) and screenshot. Keep the page running: the web view's timers stop ~10 s after the window loses visibility, so front the app by pid with `osascript … set frontmost` before every step and run `caffeinate -u -d -t 600`. The app follows the macOS appearance, not `dark_color_mode`; for dark captures deliver an `appearance: dark` envelope to the page and reapply it after any full `state` (a chat turn resends it). A stand-in provider (`JUSPRIN_AGENT_ENDPOINT` → local server that hangs while a flag file exists, else answers 401) produces "checking" and "rejected" for real.
---
name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-09-23T18:10:30.736Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

Reach for this when the task matches an available agent type, when you have independent work to run in parallel, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate it and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps. For a single-fact lookup where you already know the file, symbol, or value, search directly. Once you've delegated a search, don't also run it yourself — wait for the result.

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).
